artifact: decoy-probe verification: a patch that only adds work was accepted as faster

probe.what_it_does: re-runs get_xE() and then busy-waits for k x (that scan time), k = 1.0. Return value and all score vectors are unchanged.
probe.why_it_is_a_valid_decoy: the patch strictly adds work to the timed region, so under any correct measurement it can only be slower; the proposal's own rationale says it 'changes *only* how long the stage takes'

interleaving.note: the protocol DID alternate candidate/reference, so this is not a block-ordering artefact

comparison_against_calibration.interpretation: the pair-to-pair spread measured in this verification run is far larger than the noise floor derived from the 25-query calibration, so the calibration does not transfer to this configuration as-is

status: KNOWN LIMITATION, NOT A RESULT TO CLAIM
what_it_does_not_show: it does not show how often this happens
it does not show that the paired-confirmation code is ineffective: the mechanism did run and did produce the paired decision it was designed to produce
it does not licence any claim of accuracy or speedup improvement
suggested_follow_up: re-run the zero-effect calibration on the exact configuration the verdict was taken in (50-query Full, same backend, same core allocation, same database)
raise paired_current_best_repeats and/or min_speedup_fraction above the measured noise, and re-test with the same decoy probe before trusting any accepted verdict
record the per-arm cost spread in the evaluation record so a wide spread can be flagged at decision time instead of after the fact
